misconceptions.description: Believing any repository name will produce a user site at username.github.io, rather than the exact required name
misconceptions.trigger: learner names the repo portfolio or website and expects a root-level user site
misconceptions.feedback: A user site requires a repo named exactly username.github.io. Other names publish as project sites at /repo. Match the name to the URL you want.

misconceptions.description: Assuming GitHub Pages treats Index.HTML and index.html as the same file
misconceptions.trigger: learner ships a capitalized entry filename and gets a 404 at the root
misconceptions.feedback: GitHub Pages serves index.html in lowercase as the root. Filenames are case sensitive on the server, so match the case exactly.

misconceptions.description: Treating git push -f as a routine fix for push errors without recognizing it can overwrite teammates' commits
misconceptions.trigger: learner is told by AI to force-push a shared branch and does so without pulling first
misconceptions.feedback: Force-push rewrites shared history and can delete others' work. On a shared branch, pull and integrate first, then push normally.

misconceptions.description: Thinking that deleting or renaming a committed secret file removes the exposure, ignoring that the key remains in history and must be rotated
misconceptions.trigger: learner removes a leaked key file but does not regenerate the key
misconceptions.feedback: A committed secret lives in history. Remove and gitignore the file, then rotate the key. Treat the exposed credential as compromised.
